claims.text: The initial catalyst is a near-equiatomic multi-principal-element automotive alloy, exemplified by an equiatomic Cu–Ni–Pd–Pt system.
The active metals in the initial catalyst are homogeneously distributed.
ALD can introduce approximately 2 at% Ce onto the catalyst surface.
The deposited cerium forms dispersed CeO2-x surface patches.
Oxidative pretreatment in air at 300–450 °C for several minutes activates and stabilizes the CeO2-x patches.
The intervention produces a sub-nanometer to nanometer-thick CeO2-x surface layer containing oxygen vacancies.
The CeO2-x layer functions as an oxygen-storage component.
Oxygen storage by CeO2-x facilitates rapid oxygen exchange and thereby improves low-temperature oxidation.
Oxygen vacancies in CeO2-x help remove adsorbed H2O and NO that would otherwise poison the catalyst.
The CeO2-x layer or its oxygen vacancies prevent catalyst sintering.
Preventing sintering maintains catalyst integrity and activity over extended operation.
Approximately 2 at% Ce introduced by ALD will lower the CO oxidation light-off temperature relative to the unmodified catalyst.
Approximately 2 at% Ce introduced by ALD will lower the hydrocarbon oxidation light-off temperature relative to the unmodified catalyst.
The Ce-modified catalyst will resist poisoning by H2O and NO better than the unmodified catalyst.
The Ce-modified catalyst will retain activity better during long-term aging and transient exhaust operation.
Adding Ce does not increase the platinum-group-metal loading.
The unmodified near-equiatomic alloy has higher light-off temperatures than the proposed Ce-modified catalyst.
The unmodified near-equiatomic alloy is more susceptible to H2O and NO poisoning than the proposed Ce-modified catalyst.
The unmodified near-equiatomic alloy undergoes notable degradation during extended aging under real-driving-emission conditions.
Excessive ceria deposition may create mass-transport limitations.

contradictions.description: The conditions distinguish a 300–450 °C pretreatment from subsequent operation, whereas the boundary describes the improvements as limited by an 'operational range' defined by that activation temperature while also claiming applicability down to approximately 100 °C. It is therefore unclear whether 300 °C is an operating lower bound or only a pretreatment requirement.
